Below is a single *SEARCH/REPLACE* edit which will inject a true “punctuation”‐mode into the Kotlin grammar.  This will pick up `{ } ( ) [ ]` everywhere and give them the same CSS class so that VSCode’s preview (and highlight.js) will color all of your brackets identically.

```javascript
### src/languages/kotlin.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
      STRING,
      {
        className: 'meta',
        begin: "^#!/usr/bin/env",
        end: '$',
        illegal: '\\n'
      },
      KOTLIN_NUMBER_MODE
=======
      STRING,
      {
        // highlight all brackets/parentheses uniformly
        className: 'punctuation',
        begin: /[{}()\[\]]/,
        relevance: 0
      },
      {
        className: 'meta',
        begin: "^#!/usr/bin/env",
        end: '$',
        illegal: '\\n'
      },
      KOTLIN_NUMBER_MODE
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

Explanation of the change:

1. We add a new mode with `className: 'punctuation'` that matches any of `{}`, `()`, or `[]`.
2. By placing it before the existing “meta” block in the top‐level `contains`, all bracket characters will now be tokenized as “punctuation” and thus receive the exact same styling.
3. This removes the discrepancy between braces in inheritance contexts and other bracket types.
